::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
SMIC's original Beijing campus — 中芯北京 (registered July 2002, its first 12-inch site) and 中芯北方 (NORIC, established July 2013 with a $3.59 billion initial investment) — the mature-node workhorse the tracker had missed while covering the newer 中芯京城 JV: NORIC ran at 100.76% utilization in Jan–Aug 2025 and earned ¥11.58 billion net in 2024, SMIC's 'cash cow'.
:::

**Chinese name:** 中芯国际集成电路制造（北京）有限公司 / 中芯北方集成电路制造（北京）有限公司 (Zhōngxīn Běijīng / Zhōngxīn Běifāng)

## What does this facility make?

28nm-and-above logic, RF, embedded memory and CIS wafers on two 300mm lines.

## Why does it matter?

September 2025: SMIC announced it would buy out NORIC's remaining 49% (¥40.601 billion, share-and-cash at ¥74.20/share, valuing NORIC well above the ¥37.4 billion transaction basis); approved by the SSE M&A committee 11 May 2026 — the largest STAR-market M&A — and completed via HKEX disclosure 24 June 2026. Consolidating the mature-node cash cow inside the listed company shows how central 28nm economics have become to China's foundry champion.

## Project Timeline

- **Jul 2013** — 中芯北方 (NORIC) established; initial total investment $3.59 billion
- **Jun 2016** — First NORIC line (L1, 40/28nm) reaches production
- **Jan 2022** — Both lines combined reach 75,000 wafers/month design capacity
- **Jun 2026** — SMIC's ¥40.6 billion buyout of the remaining 49% completed — NORIC now wholly owned
